factors.name: General model size and connectivity
factors.summary: This single unrotated factor is a general factor on which every retained measure loads. Control flow complexity, Size and Number of duplicate tasks load almost perfectly (≥0.995), followed by the connector-degree and arcs-per-node measures (0.86–0.96). Larger nets in this dataset have more branching, more duplicate or silent transitions and denser connectors, while Density falls as they grow (-0.73). Separability loads only weakly (0.44, communality 0.19), so the factor explains little of it.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO is 0.73, above the 0.6 threshold. One eigenvalue clearly dominates (6.25; the next is 0.82), so a single factor was extracted. It explains 76% of the variance and reflects how the measures grow together with the size of the discovered nets. Because there is only one factor, it cannot separate distinct dimensions such as size, density or structuredness. Sequentiality and Connector Mismatch were removed for low MSA. Connector Heterogeneity, Token split and Number of empty sequence flows were constant, which suggests that concurrency-related variation is largely absent from these nets.
caveats: The near-unit loadings of Size, Control flow complexity and Number of duplicate tasks, together with the tiny last eigenvalues, indicate near-collinearity, so these measures are largely redundant in this dataset.
Separability is poorly represented by the factor (communality 0.19), so most of its variance remains unexplained.
Three measures were constant and two were removed by the MSA filter, so the result does not speak to concurrency, sequentiality or connector balance.
Bartlett's test reports 45 degrees of freedom, which corresponds to 10 measures rather than the 8 retained, so it was likely computed before the MSA filter.
The single-factor solution reflects shared variance in these 288 discovered nets and may change with other discovery algorithms, logs or a different factor count.
